The first batch of iPhone Duos are out in the wild, and a bunch of app developers are finding ways to make the most of its foldable design. Perhaps the weirdest so far is Toastie, a game that essentially turns your $2,000 device into a grilled cheese maker. Add some ingredients, close the iPhone Duo, and toast your creation to perfection.
We turned the iPhone Duo into the world’s most expensive toaster 🥪Build the sandwich quickly, then close your Duo to toast it. Don’t burn it though!Check it out: https://t.co/riRVUFLlm1 https://t.co/0llh2lv9R1
It costs $3, less than an actual grilled cheese, and for that you get "10 orders, 3 loaves, and 14 things to put between them." Your crispy masterpiece then gets a star rating for the recipe, plating, toasting, and preparation time. You can also play on iPhone and iPad without the cute close mechanic if you're more interested in browning wheat-based products than you are fooling around with a hinge.
The game is the work of Tom Szykulski and Cyprian Brytan, and they say development took place "over more evenings than either of them planned."
Apple revealed its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, back in September. If you're waiting on your delivery, check out our picks for the best iPhone Duo cases while you wait.
Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

item.title: Francis Lawrence, director of Netflix’s BioShock movie, opened up to IGN about his favorite video games of all time, and we have to admit that he knows ball.
item.description:
Francis Lawrence, director of Netflix’s BioShock movie, opened up to IGN about his favorite video games of all time, and we have to admit that he knows ball.
You might know Lawrence from his work on the Hunger Games films. He's directed almost every single one of them, after all, most recently lending his talents to the upcoming prequel film Sunrise on the Reaping, which hits theaters this November.
With a slew of blockbuster adaptations under his belt, Lawrence is now helming the live-action BioShock movie at Netflix — a project that's nearly 20 years in the making. Given he’s a self-professed fan of the series, we had to ask about his favorite games of all time.
BioShock: The Collection Screenshots
"Well, the big ones for me were Metal Gear Solid, BioShock, and Call of Duty," he answered. "I'd say the original GTA. I don't think I played beyond the original GTA, but the original one was pretty wild when that came out, the sort of technology of it. But I think those were all kind of my favorites."
When we brought up the imminent release of GTA 6 — arguably the most technologically advanced game in the franchise and one of the most highly anticipated pop culture launches of all time — Lawrence bemoaned how close the game's release is to Sunrise on the Reaping.
"Unfortunately, I think it comes out right around the same time our movie does. Hopefully, people find time for both. Play GTA, go see our movie, play more GTA," he joked.
We got the chance to chat with Lawrence about his BioShock movie, which he said was initially brought to him by Gore Verbinski back in 2009. However, due to scheduling conflicts, he wasn’t able to take the project. Guillermo del Toro was later in talks to direct the film, but "didn’t see eye-to-eye" with the game’s creator, as Lawrence put it.
The version of events that Guillermo del Toro gave to us, however, was far less mild. "We had a very contentious call about a couple of games," he told us as part of our IGN30 Icons interview series. "...So adapting it, BioShock, we had a couple of calls. They are probably one of the most disastrous calls I've ever had. So no, f**k no."
Lawrence is also gearing up to direct a film adaptation of Red Rising, a young adult book series written by author Peirce Brown. That project, too, has been in development hell, but finally found a home at Paramount and a writer to pen the script.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: We got the chance to chat with Francis Lawrence, director of the forthcoming Red Rising movie, who let us in on some exciting updates about the project and its current status at Paramount.
item.description:
We got the chance to chat with Francis Lawrence, director of the forthcoming Red Rising movie, who let us in on some exciting updates about the project and its current status at Paramount.
Francis Lawrence might as well be the end-all, be-all of young adult book-to-screen adaptations. Best known for directing almost every single movie in the Hunger Games series, Lawrence recently helmed The Long Walk and is following that up with the next Hunger Games movie, Sunrise on the Reaping, in November.
Given his extensive pedigree with YA literature adaptations, we had to quiz him about the upcoming Red Rising movie, the long-awaited adaptation of author Pierce Brown’s galaxy-spanning sci-fi epic.
Red Rising: The Board Game
According to Lawrence, multiple "regime changes" at Netflix — where the movie was first set to release — set things back, but after eight long years, it finally found a home at Paramount.
"I have been attached to Red Rising for about eight years, and Pierce [Brown] and I have become friends. The books were actually brought to me by my producing partner, Cam [MacConomy], who's a producer on this movie and has worked with me since 2010. He found the books and brought [them] to me, and I fell in love with them, and Cam is in love with them. We met with Pierce and we brought it out to market and went to Netflix. We were going to do it as a series, originally. Unfortunately, our experience at Netflix — we had two amazing pilots written, but regimes kept changing and they kept creating these departments of 'tentpole, now it's YA, back to tentpole again,'" he explained.
"It was getting bounced around, and it's not a cheap [project] to make and to do it right. They never got the guts to pull the trigger on it. And so, the rights reverted back to Pierce. Pierce then went to Paramount, which I was happy about, because I actually prefer the theatrical approach for Red Rising rather than streaming, because I think it's a series that's definitely deserving of a theatrical experience and IMAX and the whole thing.
"I'm very, very excited about that. We have a writer that we like, who is now starting work on a script, and hopefully that's something that we will put together quite quickly. It seems to be a priority at Paramount, which is great. Super, super, super excited about that. But I love the books and I love Pierce and I'm really, really excited."
Despite the news going public just two weeks ago, Lawrence has been eagerly involved in this project for almost a decade, and it — much like the highly-anticipated BioShock movie — is finally moving forward after years of red tape and production complications.
Speaking of BioShock, Lawrence opened up about the forthcoming film and gave us all the gritty details as to why it’s taken so long to get made, but assured us that, as a gamer, he’s doing everything he can to be as faithful to the source material as possible.
Image Credits: Greg Doherty/Getty Images for Lionsgate

item.title: GTA 6's release has led to as much as a 17% increase in time-off requests, according to a new report.
item.description:
GTA 6's release has led to as much as a 17% increase in time-off requests, according to a new report.
As reported by Money.com, new data from HR software company BambooHR revealed that there has been a notable spike in time-off requests for November 19. BambooHR revealed that there has been an increase between 9% to 17% on November 19, compared to normal requests for the third Thursday in November. While we aren't sure if every single person is taking that day off to play GTA 6, it stands to reason that this is what the bulk of these requests are for.
Economists have estimated a $1 billion loss in productivity in the United States due to GTA 6's release. While we'll just have to wait and see what kind of impact the game has on the world, it is clear that this is a massive event. There's a high level of anticipation for GTA 6, and it is expected to have one of the biggest entertainment launches of all time, if not the biggest.
In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023
Rockstar has also been spending a ton of money to get the word out with extravagant marketing; it spent $975,000 to install a massive neon pink sign on top of the Miami Heat's arena, after all. The developer also covered the city with in-universe ads for brands in the game, along with more traditional banners featuring the game's key art. Fans can even eat at a real life version of Burger Shot, a fast food chain in the GTA universe, if they live in Miami.
There will also be an unprecedented NBA game between the Miami Heat and the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18, which will turn the Heat into the Vice City Heat. They will play with GTA 6-themed jerseys on a never-before-seen Vice City court. It should be quite the spectacle, and serve as an effective final marketing beat for the game.
GTA 6 will release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A PC port is also rumored for early 2027.

item.title: Composer Austin Wintory was once in talks to make music for Mass Effect 5, and now that EA has shuttered BioWare and canceled the game, he's released his drafts online.
item.description:
Composer Austin Wintory was once in talks to make music for Mass Effect 5. Now that EA has shuttered BioWare and canceled the game, he's released his drafts online.
The award-winning composer behind Sword of the Sea, Journey, and a laundry list of other video games, movies, and shows revealed that he had been in talks to create music for the now-canceled Mass Effect revival in a post on social media. Whether he would have gone on to officially create music for what was in development under the name Mass Effect: Universe is unclear, but judging by the 22 minutes of audio published online for fans, it's clear there was some weight behind those early talks.
Wintory called Mass Effect an "all-time dream project" that never came to be. Any hope to continue working on the series seems to have been dashed, which is why any drafts he managed to drum up can now be found on YouTube. It's yet another sneak peek at a project that will likely never see the light of day, and unfortunately for the millions of Mass Effect fans still out there, it's quite good.
So here you go ... Thank you again to my friends at both BioWare and EA. To even dream in your sandbox was a privilegehttps://t.co/wmq2N7s6Kp
"Working on Mass Effect 5 was my career's biggest dream project, my white whale," he said in the description of his YouTube upload. "It is my favorite franchise of all time, and for the last couple years I'd been in serious conversations with BioWare and EA to jump in. My suggestion was to treat the original game's masterful Jack Wall / Sam Hulick score as a starting point, and to build on it from there with deeper use of physical, analog synths, and a more tightly interwoven use of the orchestra. But a love letter first and foremost (not unlike my approach to the Aliens franchise with Fireteam Elite)."
Wintory explained that it was during these talks his excitement led him to surprise EA and BioWare with an "elaborate production" consisting of 20 minutes of music for whatever the next Mass Effect would become. Its plot details were a mystery at the time, with the composer clarifying that the music we hear today is "just pure musical exploration."
Still, his past as a Mass Effect fan, which dates all the way back to the release of the original game in 2007, is pretty easy to feel. Wintory added that it was "fully recorded and produced with synths, vocals, and a large orchestra" in Los Angeles. It may have been reworked, rearranged, or maybe even scrapped altogether by the time an official release rolled around, but that didn't stop the composer from putting his heart into it.
Every IGN Mass Effect Review
"Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss," he added. "It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever."
In follow-up posts on social media, Wintory said he hopes his drafts do justice to the work of Wall and Hulick, calling his unofficial entry in the Mass Effect universe a "pure love letter." He added, "So here you go ... Thank you again to my friends at both BioWare and EA. To even dream in your sandbox was a privilege."
BioWare's demise has rocked the games industry. After decades of delivering some of the most groundbreaking stories gaming has ever seen, EA announced it would be closing the studio and canceling its Mass Effect 5 last week. Even if it's bittersweet, leaked materials have emerged in the wake of the studio's closure, giving everyone a peek behind the curtain not only at what could have been but just how far along development managed to get.
Did you play through the entire Mass Effect Trilogy? If so, which was your favorite?

item.title: Ubisoft has detailed Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced's final major content update, revealing a closer look at new game+, Nightmare difficulty, and more.
item.description:
Ubisoft has detailed Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced's final major content update, revealing a closer look at new game+, Nightmare difficulty, and more.
The publisher behind the Assassin's Creed 4 remake broke down some of the most-requested features finally set to make their way to players in a video published today. It's one last push that's set to drop tomorrow, October 27, to keep players plundering before Edward Kenway sails off into the sunset yet again.
New game+ and Nightmare difficulty are no doubt the highlights here. The first addition is mostly self-explanatory, allowing players to start a new save file with all of the tools they gathered from a previous, completed playthrough. It supports up to new game+ 5 and, as detailed by game director Richard Knight, gives players "plenty of opportunities to push your skills to the limit and unlock exclusive rewards."
If running it back through the West Indies isn't enough of a challenge, there's Nightmare difficulty. A description for the harder mode's version of Activities, for example, says that "harpooning preys are the most vicious" and "underwater breath is very limited." In addition to making Edward's journey more dangerous, the final major content update is "more spectacular" thanks to a collection of new takedown animations.
"And that's not all," Knight said. "Alongside these new features, we've also added new Easter Eggs, a host of rewards to discover – including community-inspired trinkets – new outfits, sails, and even adorable new pet cat skins.
"Thank you for your support, fan art, videos, and millions of photos shared in photo mode. It was a real honor to bring back Edward's legacy to life and to see that same excitement find its echo amongst you throughout the year."
Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced Screenshots
Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced launched for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S July 9, 2026. IGN gave it a 9/10 review, saying, "More than just a shinier version of the same game you remember, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced brings what was already one of the best games in the series up to today’s standards."
Title update 1.0.8 will indeed be the final major content update when it launches tomorrow, but Ubisoft may continue to deliver smaller quality-of-life fixes should the opportunity arise. Until then, you can see what percentage of players have struggled to take down those infamous Legendary Ships.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

As streaming services gear up for the holiday season, HBO Max has announced a particularly exciting addition for Studio Ghibli fans: the return of Calcifer's Yule Log. A Warner Bros. press release confirms the ambient video will be making its return to streaming on November 1.
While Calcifer's Yule Log first debuted in HBO Max during the 2021 holiday season, it was later removed from the service and largely scraped from the internet. It returns briefly during the holiday season each year as part of HBO Max's "Yule Log" lineup, which has grown to include properties like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, Harry Potter, and even Rick and Morty.
Warner Bros. has yet to confirm whether the video will remain on the service permanently, or will once again be removed after the holiday season.
The Best Studio Ghibli Movies
Howl’s Moving Castle was first published as a book by one of the most influential fantasy authors, Diana Wynne Jones. The Studio Ghibli adaptation, directed by Hayao Miyazaki, was released in theaters in 2004. It’s since grown into one of the animation studio's most popular properties, serving as the basis for tons of merchandise and entire sections of the Ghibli Park. We consider it one of the best Studio Ghibli movies of all time.
Calcifer, who was voiced by Tatsuya Gashuin in the original release and Billy Crystal in the English dub, quickly became one of the most popular characters in the animated adaptation. The flaming creature quite literally powers Howl’s titular moving castle, and despite his sassy remarks, offers a surprising amount of warmth in his relationships with Howl and Sophie.
While the Yule Log video doesn’t quite focus on the spirit’s boisterous personality, it’s a pleasant holiday offering for Studio Ghibli fans. The 30-minute video, inspired by the "virtual fireplace" trend, shows Calcifer peacefully keeping Howl's fireplace lit alongside music and ambient noises from the film.
What is the best Studio Ghibli movie of all time?

item.title: We got the chance to sit down with Francis Lawrence, the director of Netflix’s in-development BioShock movie, who gave us some of the gritty details as to why this adaptation has taken so long to make.
item.description:
We got the chance to sit down with Francis Lawrence, the director of Netflix’s BioShock movie, who gave us some of the gritty details as to why this adaptation has taken so long to make.
The BioShock movie is a project that’s been floating in limbo for more than a decade. The film initially had Gore Verbinski (Pirates of the Caribbean) attached to direct, but it fell through. Later, Guillermo del Toro was in talks to helm the steampunk movie, but that didn’t work out, either.
Now, Lawrence — who directed almost every Hunger Games movie and, most recently, The Long Walk — is taking over. Lawrence chatted about his history with the BioShock movie in an interview for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which comes to theaters next month. When asked about what projects he’d like to adapt in the future, he mentioned BioShock but admitted it’s been “tricky” to translate to the silver screen.
BioShock: The Collection Screenshots
“I'm also working on BioShock. That's another one that I've been really trying to get going, which is also at Netflix, which is partially tricky. That's a tricky adaptation, because it's an amazing, amazing world. But as a player, you are the lead character of that story. So cracking that is a tough one, but we're getting close, which is also exciting,” he told us.
Lawrence admitted the film has been in his orbit since 2009, saying that Verbinski actually approached him about it — essentially offering it up to him on a silver platter — after his vision for the movie was shot down by Universal.
“This thing has kind of been on my radar for a long time, as was The Long Walk," he continued. "The Long Walk was something that I tried to do probably 20 years ago, and then somebody else got the rights, and then it kind of bounced around, bounced around, bounced around, and I sort of tracked it, and then it finally landed in my lap, and I went and made it. I remember BioShock was around 2009, I think Gore Verbinski was going to do it at Universal. But it was a $200 million movie, and he wanted a very specific person in it that was not a star, and it was R-rated. Universal was like, ‘No way are we doing this.’ So Gore actually approached me and asked if I wanted to do it, but I was already doing something else and couldn't.
“So since probably 2009, it's kind of been in my orbit and something that's always been percolating a little bit like Long Walk. And then yeah, when Guillermo didn't see eye to eye with some of the — I think it was the creator of the game — and that kind of fell apart, then it came my direction. And so I sort of jumped at the opportunity and so I have been trying to develop that one.”
Lawrence’s remark about del Toro not seeing “eye to eye” with BioShock’s creator is a gentle way of putting their conversation; speaking with IGN earlier this year, del Toro told us that he never wants to try his hand at adapting a video game ever again, citing a “disastrous” phone call he had with the folks behind BioShock as the reason why.
“We had a very contentious call about a couple of games,” he recalled. “...So adapting it, BioShock, we had a couple of calls. They are probably one of the most disastrous calls I've ever had. So no, f**k no.”
Lawrence assured us that he's dedicated to making the movie the best it can be, telling us that he's focused on honoring the source material and making sure the game is faithfully brought to the screen as best it can be.
"The creator of BioShock had to basically just give the sign off on me, my knowledge," he said. "Again, [he] wanted to know that I was in love with the spirit of the game. I think he wanted to really protect certain elements and ideas and themes, as one should if you're the creator."
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Collectibles creator The Loyal Subjects has released the game's first official toy collection, featuring everything from articulated figures to mystery eggs.
item.description:
It's a good time to be a Palworld obsessive. The game recently teased its next update, Palworld: Side by Side, coming this winter, and now collectibles creator The Loyal Subjects has released the game's first official toy collection, featuring everything from articulated figures to mystery eggs. It's available now on Amazon.
Decorate your desk with the frankly adorable Chillet, take everyone's favorite oversized electric menace Grizzbolt out and about, and keep the perpetually vacant-looking Relaxasaurus in your pocket to remind you not to scream at your boss.
There are four different products in the collection, starting with a range of 4-inch articulated figures featuring Foxparks, Relaxasaurus, Grizzbolt, and Lifmunk. Each comes with its own Battle FX accessory, so you can make them fight without having to worry about a raid on your base.
For those who prefer their Pals a little smaller, because it's not the size of the Pal that matters but what you do with it that counts, there's also a 3-inch collector set featuring Chillet, Grizzbolt, and Relaxasaurus (see at Amazon).
And because apparently collecting Pals in the game wasn't enough, there are two different mystery collections to hunt down. The Cheebee Micro Blind Mystery Pal Egg 12-Pack includes a dozen 1.5-inch mystery figures, while the Blind Egg Incubator Reveal 8-Pack offers eight miniature Pals to hatch and collect.
As always, the blind-box format means there's no guarantee you'll get the Pal you're after, so happy hunting to all the completionists out there. At least these ones won't require you to craft hundreds of Pal Spheres.
The collection is available to pre-order now on Amazon.

item.title: The canceled movie spinoff is getting a new lease of life as Playable Archive, released today for free on Steam.
item.description:
Every horror fan knows the rule: Just when you think the monster is dead, they always come back. The game Paranormal Activity: Threshold is no exception, with the canceled movie spinoff getting a new lease on life as Playable Archive, which is released today, for free, on Steam.
It's your classic tale of a young couple simply trying to do some renovations on their home and ending up paying the price for tampering with a strange object they came across during their remodel. The story is told through found footage and ticks all the spooky boxes with rituals, strange symbols, and shaky camera footage with an ominous entity just out of shot.
The original Paranormal Activity project was killed earlier this year by Paramount, but developer Brian Clarke, who made the jump-scare joy The Mortuary Assistant, worked with publisher DreadXP to resurrect a new version of the game available to horror fans.
"I have to admit, I was feeling burnt out, and I imagined the project would simply sit on a shelf forever. A forgotten relic of development that sat in darkness while I built up a plan for a new project," Clarke said in a Steam post. "DreadXP reached out to me and floated the idea of maybe releasing what I had. It felt like a good way of laying the project to rest instead of remaining a lingering ghost. So, I worked to adjust the project where needed and polished up the edges to release the work I had done. I’m sad to say that a good deal of work was still left on the cutting room floor, but I’m proud of what I am able to share and that it is going to see the light of day in some form."
The game has no save system and needs to be played in one sitting, according to the Steam listing, so be prepared to lock in.
If you're sad about the Paranormal Activity part of it, don't worry; you only have to wait until next year for a new Paranormal Activity movie from James Wan.

item.title: Cygnus Cross, the development team behind the promising "Diablo meets Stardew Valley" game Emberville, has delayed their Early Access launch the day before it was supposed to happen. The new Early Access release date is January 7, 2027. To soften the blow the team says that the content originally planned for its first major post-launch update will now be included in the January 7 Early Access release.
item.description:
Cygnus Cross, the development team behind the promising "Diablo meets Stardew Valley" game Emberville, has delayed their Early Access launch the day before it was supposed to happen. The new Early Access release date is January 7, 2027. To soften the blow, the team says that the content originally planned for its first major post-launch update will now be included in the January 7 Early Access release.
"We know this is very short notice, with launch just a day away," Cygnus Cross wrote in a press release. "After extensive discussions within the team, we have made the difficult decision to postpone Emberville’s Early Access release. Many of you have played our Steam Next Fest demo and shared your feedback. This means a great deal to us, and we immediately started planning more improvements. However, some of the improvements we want to make are systems changes that can't be done quickly. Reworking bow combat, for example, would take more time than we had prior to our Early Access release, even though the team is working around the clock.
"After carefully considering our options, we have decided to move the release date and include some essential improvements in the Early Access launch build. We understand that this will be disappointing for those of you who were ready to buy the game. While we could have simply released the game now, we feel that it wouldn’t be up to our standards and to your high expectations of us." The team concluded with, "Once Early Access begins, we will follow up with regular updates, both large and small. We will continue adding content, listening to your ideas and suggestions, and building Emberville together with you. Thank you for your support, patience and understanding."
We really liked what we played in our most recent hands-on preview of Emberville if you'd like to check that out. You can also wishlist it on Steam if you're interested.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: The Batman Part 2 star Robert Pattinson has called Steven Soderbergh stepping in to help finish the film a "selfless" act.
item.description:
The Batman Part 2 star Robert Pattinson has called Steven Soderbergh stepping in to help finish the film a "selfless" act.
Earlier this month, it was revealed that Steven Soderbergh would be stepping in to help finish The Batman Part 2. Director Matt Reeves ultimately had to step away from the film during its final weeks of production for a personal matter, and Soderbergh offered to help get principal photography across the finish line. He will then pass the baton back to Reeves, who will handle the post-production process.
It's a unique situation, but one that Soderbergh is doing to help Reeves deliver on his vision. It's not a case of a studio getting rid of one guy to bring in a yes-man to carry out their wishes; it's a friend helping out a pal during a tough time.
The Batman: Part II - Who's Who in Matt Reeves' DC Sequel
When speaking with GamesRadar, Pattinson addressed the situation and spoke highly of Soderbergh for helping out on The Batman Part 2.
“I am so happy he’s come on to help Matt,” Pattinson said of Soderbergh. “It’s incredibly generous of him – and he’s doing it in the loveliest way. It’s completely selfless. I think Matt had put so much work into the script, and we’re almost done. So for someone to come in and say, ‘I just want to help Matt do it; I want to do it in conjunction with him and just get it to the edit.’ And to have someone who’s as talented as Steven doing it is great.”
Pattinson also noted that filming has resumed, and he is expected to return to set as Bruce Wayne/Batman next week. The film's story remains tightly under wraps, as we don't even know who the villains are. Sebastian Stan is expected to play one of the antagonists and has long been rumored for Harvey Dent, but his shaved head has made fans wonder if that's accurate. Scarlett Johansson is also confirmed to have a large role, but it's unclear who she will play or what side of the moral spectrum she will be on.
The Batman Part 2 is slated to hit theaters on February 18, 2026.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: The Call of Duty franchise has now surpassed $40 billion in lifetime franchise revenue in the wake of the launch of its 23rd mainline entry, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which launched last Friday.
item.description:
The Call of Duty franchise has now surpassed $40 billion in lifetime franchise revenue in the wake of the launch of its 23rd mainline entry, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which launched last Friday.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma made the announcement on her X account, posting a graphic showing a bunch of favorable review scores for Modern Warfare 4 with the caption, "One of the most celebrated Call of Duty games in its 24-year history, and now $40B in lifetime franchise revenue. An incredible milestone. Congrats to the Activision team. And to the players, thank you for being with us."
The staying power of the franchise has been remarkably impressive, even if some years' releases are more liked by critics and players than other years. The brand-new Modern Warfare 4 seems to be well-received so far; IGN hasn't finalized its review yet, but reviewer Simon Cardy says, "Modern Warfare 4’s campaign made me feel something for the series again" and "its expansive behind-enemy-lines mission that borrows most of its ideas from the DMZ mode is a real highlight."
For context, Grand Theft Auto 5 alone has pulled in over $10 billion over the past 13 years, and the imminent GTA 6 is estimated to clear $5.2 billion by the end of its first week on sale.
Call of Duty will soon expand beyond just games, however, as Peter Berg's Call of Duty movie is due out in theaters on June 30, 2028 and will explore "the cost of war" for its characters.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Mass Effect fans have bought a #SaveMassEffect billboard in Times Square after EA shut down BioWare last week, but the fight to save the sci-fi RPG franchise isn't stopping there.
item.description:
Mass Effect fans have bought a #SaveMassEffect billboard in Times Square after EA shut down BioWare last week, but the fight to save the sci-fi RPG franchise isn't stopping there.
Whether New York City residents are familiar with Commander Shepard's fight against the Reapers or not, everyone in Times Square was alerted to #SaveMassEffect when its billboard went up today. It's the latest in a string of moves from the community backing the sci-fi RPG franchise and its developers as they work to give them a second wind.
"Keelah si'yah," text on the billboard said. It's a reference to the in-universe language of Khelish, which is spoken by the Quarian species. According to the Mass Effect Wiki, the line specifically translates to "by the homeworld I hope to find one day."
🚨 WE'RE IN TIMES SQUARE!Together with @kalaelizabeth, we've managed to get a #SaveMassEffect billboard up in Times Square, NYC, all day today!📍 1560 Broadway, above the Pelé store (Duffy Square)⏰ 15 seconds every hour at :35HOLD THE LINE! ❤️ https://t.co/wNP9Ak9Vh8
Those supporting #SaveMassEffect come from all over, but the billboard featured in Times Square on this late-October day came from a smaller group known as We Are Mass Effect, a community dedicated to paying tribute to the franchise started in summer 2025 by a 27-year-old in Spain named Ariel Peña Aguilar. He, along with his second-in-command, Mer, as well as X/Twitter user Kala Elizabeth, sought to publish the billboard in hopes of drawing attention to their cause.
The idea originally came from Aguilar and Mer before Elizabeth was brought in for assistance and is part of their goal to keep Mass Effect alive. So far, their efforts include emailing EA directly, contacting Canadian politicians, and doing everything they can to draw more attention to their cause. The best part? Their Times Square billboard is just the beginning.
Aguilar told IGN that community organization around canceled Star Wars project The Hunt for Ben Solo is partly what inspired his push to save Mass Effect. He added, "I thought something like that could work really well for our situation, too."
Our beloved @drowwpoison, co-ceo of We Are Mass Effect, who's been working incredibly hard to give the #SaveMassEffect movement even more power, went to see our billboard in Times Square, New York City! ❤️✍️ Sign the petition: https://t.co/AhcEFDBbd0 https://t.co/69jfSoxyci
"At first, I thought it might be a bit of a crazy idea," Aguilar said of the billboard, "but then I brought it up with my project partner, Mer, and the incredible content creator Kala Elizabeth, without whom none of this would have been possible. We all agreed it was worth doing, and we started organizing everything. And we have more plans! The billboard is just the first step."
There's a natural question that comes up whenever there's a grassroots push like this: How much does it cost to put up a billboard in Times Square? Well, at least on a Monday in October, it's only about $250. Both Aguilar and Elizabeth confirmed the financial cost of boosting #SaveMassEffect wasn't the issue. Instead, it was copyright hangups that gave them more trouble than anything, even if it's now a "fun anecdote," according to Aguilar.
"We initially had someone else make a different graphic, but it said 'BioWare' in it, so we had to change it last minute because of copyright," Elizabeth told us. "There was a lot of back-and-forth in a rush to fix it, and I had to remake it myself. I did end up using the wrong Mass Effect saying because I've been thinking about the author Catherynne Valente, who announced she had been working on Mass Effect 5, and she had written a previous novel about the Quarian ark for Andromeda. Keelah si'yah is that ark. It's still somewhat fitting of the intent, but we mean keelah se'lai. Oops."
Lots of great feedback in the comments. Our next billboard will be simpler and include a QR code to the petition!
As if there was ever any doubt, there are millions of people who still care about Mass Effect. Aguilar clarified that We Are Mass Effect isn't directly affiliated with the major petition going around, even if they do "fully support the petition and the effort behind it." For him, they are "simply fans trying to use every tool and resource at our disposal to support the cause and make sure this movement continues for as long as possible."
Aguilar sees the joint effort as "a message of unity" in the aftermath of decisions made by EA "that goes far beyond our concern for Mass Effect or Dragon Age." This is about more than video games.
"At the end of the day," Aguilar added, "these franchises are works of art, and while they mean an enormous amount to us, we're also deeply concerned about all the developers who have lost their jobs, as well as those who may still face layoffs in the future, especially during such a difficult period for the video game industry."
Every IGN Mass Effect Review
He continued: "They're the ones who deserve our support the most. We're going to hold the line." It should be said, though, that no one here is under the illusion that EA has any intention of changing course – or even listening.
As Mass Effect fans work together for another trip among the stars, dissenting opinions have seen naysayers push back against any hope at a revival. Aguilar mentioned the billboard team is "familiar with EA's track record when it comes to how they treat their IPs and developers," adding, "it's easy to understand why fans would feel defeated from the outset." Even if expecting change from EA is a "naïve and unrealistic expectation," they'll continue to push forward anyway.
"Unfortunately, I think we all know that EA probably does not care," Elizabeth added, "but amidst all the horrible press right now around EA's new owners, Jared Kushner and the Saudi government, I hope their track record of killing games becomes another topic of the conversation. This is, albeit, just a small part of the corrupt government and sports washing conversation around EA's new owners, but is absolutely part of it.
The #SaveMassEffect petition just hit 200,000! Absolutely insane work by everyone, keep it up! ♥️ https://t.co/tHiNeNhmCt
"SaveMassEffect is also about trying to save media. History. BioWare was a pillar of Edmonton for 30 years, and EA bought them out and shut them down like they have done for now 20 studios. I don't want them to sit on IPs and let them die. Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and Dead Space are just a few, and they all deserve better. What happens when this massive debt they've accrued closes EA, too? Then what?
"This is about the preservation of media and preserving the work of the studios that EA keeps killing. We don't even know if EA let BioWare try to buy themselves out or let someone else buy them before they closed the studio, canceled the game, and fired the 50 employees keeping BioWare together. What they're doing is wrong. BioWare deserved better. The employees deserved better, and the fans deserve better, too.
"We are probably looking at a future where EA is going to sit on these IPs while they let them die but still make merchandise of Commander Shepard. All while Andrew Wilson collects his massive yearly bonuses and lets EA turn into an esports-only company controlled by the Saudi government."
The Art of Dragon Age: The Veilguard - Preview Gallery
What comes next for the movement at large isn't totally clear, but We Are Mass Effect has a few tricks left up its sleeve. Elizabeth said one plan is to launch a GoFundMe, "with the intent that if people donate a few dollars without breaking their banks in this economy, we can get some more mobile billboards to spread the word." Even if BioWare and Mass Effect are truly gone, even if the efforts of #SaveMassEffect yield no change, there is hope for the future. November 7, 2027, marks 20 years of Mass Effect, and even if EA doesn't celebrate it, Elizabeth knows the fans, voice actors, and developers will.
"I know they care and they're still going to be here for the fans who aren't going anywhere," she continued. "Support them, support the devs, support the people who lost their jobs and their work to the void.
"I hope something comes out of this, and if it doesn't, at least we tried, right?"
SPREAD THE WORD ‼️ THIS IS JUST THE BEGINNING, N7 4 EVER ❤️🖤 #SaveMassEffect https://t.co/wMEd7DQF4u
The #SaveMassEffect billboard will be available for New York citizens to see in Times Square all day today. It will appear for 15 seconds every hour at the 35-minute mark on 1560 Broadway just above the Pelé Soccer store.
As the movement takes Mass Effect from the Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies and centers it on Midtown Manhattan, calls for EA to reverse course have only grown in size. That's thanks in part to a petition, which, after gaining 50,000 signatures in just a few hours, as ballooned to include 220,000 names. That includes support from game developers, Destiny fans, and even Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, with many others calling for fans to boycott EA-made titles.
After the Mass Effect trilogy altered the course of RPG gaming in the 2000s and early 2010s, the series came to an end with Mass Effect: Andromeda in 2017. BioWare continued to work on a follow-up for the franchise, working under the title Mass Effect: Universe, for years before it, too, was canceled last week.
Did you play through the entire Mass Effect Trilogy? If so, which was your favorite?

item.title: According to a comment from a cast member, all actors involved in the 2026 Street Fighter movie signed on for three films — something that helps its cliffhanger ending make a lot more sense now.
item.description:
According to a comment from a cast member, all actors involved in the 2026 Street Fighter movie signed on for three films — something that helps its cliffhanger ending make a lot more sense now.
Olivier Richters, the 7-foot-2 actor who played Zangief, revealed the news in a YouTube comment on October 25. This comment was in response to a fan video complaining that viewers didn’t get to see very much of the Red Cyclone in the film.
While this fact is objectively true, Richters explained that his brief appearance in the movie was intentional, saying this was done to make viewers extra eager for a sequel to see more of him and his invincible iron body in another installment.
Street Fighter Images
“When they asked me to play Zangief, it was all very clear. There was one goal: Show a [glimpse] of Zangief and his power, so we all want more," he wrote. "All actors, including me, signed for three movies. ‘If a sequel is made, Zangief will shine,’ was the promise. Apart from that, you can't expect, from a two-hour movie with so many characters, for everyone to shine in the first part. But anyways, thanks for wanting to see more of Zangief!”
In the Street Fighter movie, Zangief appears in two sequences — one where he receives an invitation to join the second World Warrior tournament courtesy of Chun-Li, and another where he brawls with Ken and company in a club fight.
Almost all of his moves in this second scene are taken directly from the games, and his finisher was performed practically. It was a delightful treat for players to see, and the overwhelming sentiment from fans was that they’d hoped to see more from him… and from the actual World Warrior Tournament, in general.
However, given the movie’s post-credits scene and its abrupt ending, it’s clear that Legendary’s Street Fighter movie was intended as the first in a series of films, and it set things up for a direct sequel. While we won’t spoil that here, you can check out our ending explained article for more details.
The cast has been open about wanting to film more Street Fighter movies, in large part due to how fun the first was to make — but given this latest revelation, it seems that not being able to do so would put a major damper on the studio’s plan for a trilogy.
Street Fighter’s battle at the box office has been modest; with a reported budget of around $80 million, it topped the domestic box office on its opening weekend with $51 million. As of October 26, it has grossed $79 million worldwide, meaning that it’s just shy of making back its budget.
With more time left in theaters and a streaming run in the future, it's looking likely that this movie will end up being a profit for Legendary — if a moderate one. We’ll just have to see if a sequel does, indeed, get greenlit, and if plans remain in place for a trilogy.
In the meantime, you can check out our interview with the Street Fighter cast, who told us that they are more than enthusiastic about a possible crossover flick with the Mortal Kombat crew.

item.title: Microsoft plans to offer buyouts to about 60,000 workers as part of the company’s efforts to trim costs and retool its workforce as it invests heavily in AI. That amounts to just over a quarter of its total staff.
item.description:
Microsoft plans to offer buyouts to about 60,000 workers as part of the company’s efforts to trim costs and retool its workforce as it invests heavily in AI. That amounts to just over a quarter of its total staff.
Select personnel in the U.S., Canada, the UK, and India at the vice president level and below will be eligible for a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO), Amy Coleman, Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer, said in a note to staff today. Microsoft had 223,000 employees as of the end of June, a number that was down from 228,000 at the end of 2025.
According to Bloomberg, the cuts come amid a focus on AI, with costly data centers supplying cloud services to the likes of Anthropic and OpenAI. In June, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella addressed community backlash to the company's massive AI data center buildout, which has sparked concern over power costs, environmental concerns, and the potential impact on jobs. He insisted one of Microsoft's data centers' daily water usage over the course of an entire year is roughly equivalent to what a single restaurant would use. Some staff at Microsoft, including those working on data centers, are excluded from the buyout offer.
Every Video Game Franchise Xbox Owns After Acquiring Activision Blizzard
According to CNBC, employees have until December to decide whether they will take the offer, and those who do will leave Microsoft on December 31.
The buyout offer comes just three months after Microsoft laid off 4,800 roles, or what was about 2.1% of its global workforce. The Xbox layoffs, which hit 1,600 staff in July as part of Asha Sharma's "reset" of the gaming business, formed a part of those cuts. Earlier this month, an Xbox business strategist claimed that everyone in the video games industry was using AI while pretending not to.
And earlier this year, more than 30% of eligible employees chose to to take Microsoft's first ever voluntary retirement program.
Photo by Oliver Berg/picture alliance via Getty Images.

item.title: Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch has laid off some staff, just a little over a year after the release of its last game.
item.description:
Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch has laid off some staff, just a little over a year after the release of its last game.
Aftermath reported that the studio let 26 employees go, just weeks after Ghost of Yotei's DLC and Complete Edition were released on PS5. The studio has roughly 200 employees as it stands. Aftermath shared an email that was sent out to the team from studio leadership, which reveals that "challenges in the market" and changes in the scope of the team for its next project were the deciding factors in the layoffs.
“After carefully observing the challenges in the market and reviewing the team needs for our next project, we've decided to make some staffing reductions. Several positions across Sucker Punch will be eliminated as a result," the email reads.
Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition Screenshots
The note also stated that they will discuss the plans for the studio's future next week.
”We know this is a lot to take in, and we want to assure you that we did not make this decision lightly. We have given this a lot of attention and worked to support our affected colleagues during this transition as well as we can. … There's no getting around that this is a hard day. Next week we will go into more details about the future.”
As of right now, it's unclear what Sucker Punch's next game will be; it does sound like there is another project in the cards based on the studio's statement. Some want a return to Infamous, whether through a collection of remasters/remakes or a brand-new entry. Others want a new Sly Cooper. And of course, there's appetite for more games in the studio's Ghost series. It wouldn't be surprising if at least one of these happens, as new IP with a big AAA budget is becoming harder and harder to justify.
Ghost of Yotei was one of the biggest games of fall 2025, selling 3.3 million copies in its first month. It's also one of the best-reviewed PS5 exclusives to date. It was also expected to come to PC at some point, but unfortunately, that plan was scrapped when Sony opted to move away from PC. The game recently got a Complete Edition, which added a brand-new story DLC and other additional content. It's unclear if this moved any significant copies or if the audience for the game already capped out with its initial release.
The layoffs also come during a tumultuous time for PlayStation, which has been upsetting fans over its controversial shift to an all-digital future starting in 2028. The company will phase out physical copies of games in favor of digital releases, likely beginning with PS6. PlayStation also shuttered Bluepoint, a beloved studio that was best known for high-quality remasters, ports, and remakes such as Demon's Souls for PS5. Additionally, PlayStation attempted to scrap development on Hideo Kojima's next gen game, Physint, until Microsoft swooped in to save it.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Walter Koenig, who played Chekov on the original Star Trek series, has died at age 90. Koenig joined the NBC series Star Trek in its second season as Russian crewmember Ensign Pavel Andreievich Chekov.
item.description:
Walter Koenig, who played Chekov on the original Star Trek series, has died at age 90.
“The late actor's rep tells us ... Walter's daughter, Danielle, and his niece were by his side when he died of old age at his home in North Hollywood on Sunday,” TMZ reports.
Koenig joined the NBC series Star Trek in its second season as the USS Enterprise’s Russian crewmember Ensign Pavel Andreievich Chekov. With his Beatles-style mop of hair, the boyish Chekov was meant to appeal to younger viewers a la Davy Jones of The Monkees.
As Chekov, Koenig would appear in the latter two seasons of the original series and then in all six feature films featuring the cast.
With Koenig’s death, only William Shatner (Captain Kirk) and George Takei (Mr. Sulu) remain alive from the original cast.
Takei took to social media to salute his longtime co-star:
Marvin Walter Koenig was born in Chicago on Sept. 14, 1936. The Hollywood Reporter recounts that he studied at Neighborhood Playhouse in New York alongside future sci-fi and comedy icon Christopher Lloyd, who would star opposite Koenig in Star Trek III: The Search for Spock.
After Star Trek was canceled – and the character of Chekov was left out of the animated series – Koenig turned to writing episodic television series.
Following Star Trek, Koenig returned to the sci-fi genre with his role as Alfred Bester on Babylon 5. In 2017, Koenig reprised the role of Chekov (as “The Admiral”) for the crowdsourced online series Renegades.
Koenig was widowed in 2022 after the death of his wife Judy. His son, Growing Pains actor Andrew Koenig, committed suicide in 2010.
You can read our archival interview with the Trek legend from 2024 where he looked back on the good, the bad, and the hilarious after 57 years of the franchise.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: Sony may have exclusive access to AMD's next-generation graphics architecture for a potential PlayStation handheld, the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said.
item.description:
Sony may have exclusive access to AMD's next-generation graphics architecture for a potential PlayStation handheld, the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said.
There have been rumors of a next-generation PlayStation handheld for some time now, after the success of the Nintendo Switch and a wide gamut of PC gaming handhelds. Indeed, in June, Sony Interactive Entertainment CEO Hideaki Nishino suggested PlayStation may move towards more hybrid, Switch-like consoles in the future to match modern on-the-go players.
When I watched the latest Patreon-exclusive DF Direct, Digital Foundry's Richard Leadbetter claimed that "there's been some behind-the-scenes discussion that Sony has an exclusive of sorts with AMD for RDNA 5 for handheld," and that the only other, presumably handheld, chip he knows of in production at AMD is what's going to be known as Z3, which is unlikely to have RDNA 5 graphics.
The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time
AMD and Sony have been working closely for the last couple of years, teaming up on an initiative called 'Project Amethyst,' which ultimately resulted in both PSSR 2 on the PS5 Pro and FSR 4.1 for PC and Xbox.
Speaking of Xbox, it sounds like Microsoft has handheld gaming plans of its own. Project Helix will include a whole range of devices, we were recently told, and a handheld will reportedly be the first out the gate. Fortune recently reported that Microsoft plans to release a handheld by holiday 2027, with the next-gen console following in 2028. The chips going into either of these platforms hasn't been confirmed, but AMD did come out and tease that FSR Diamond would be launching with Project Helix – of which the handheld is a part of – and that would likely be running on RDNA 5.
AMD would have reason to supercharge its handheld chip offerings for a wide range of devices, as well. Intel's Panther Lake handheld chip launched at Computex 2026 and, at least in my testing, absolutely bodies the AMD Ryzen Z2 Extreme. The Z2 Extreme only uses an RDNA 3.5 GPU, which was already an older architecture when it launched last year. The Intel Arc G3, on the other hand, uses the same GPU that powers its latest laptops, just with a few of the CPU cores disabled.
With how expensive handhelds have become lately, the whole category is in danger of vanishing until the RAM crisis abates, and so it's possible that Sony's handheld is the only one that springs for the added cost of RDNA 5. But, unless Sony inks some kind of exclusive deal with AMD, I am sure other devices using RDNA 5 will exist eventually – maybe even Xbox's own first-party handheld.
This isn’t the first PlayStation handheld tease, either. Last year, Moore’s Law Is Dead reported on an unannounced PS6 handheld that would be dockable and backwards compatible with PS4 and PS5 games. There was also a brief mention of what was described as a PS6 S, which sounded like it could be to the PS6 what the Xbox Series S is to the Xbox Series X. If true, you’d assume it would be a cheaper option.
Are you interested in handheld options for next-gen PlayStation and Xbox consoles?
